axes.model_access:
**Models are fully self-configured — this is its most core positioning.**

Providers listed on the official model providers page:

- Anthropic
- Azure AI Foundry
- Amazon Bedrock
- DeepSeek
- Gemini
- Mistral
- **Ollama (local models)**
- OpenAI
- Vertex AI
- xAI

That page also points to "More (30 items)".

Configuration lives in `config.yaml` under `models`, with fields `provider` + `model` + `apiBase`.

`roles` (chat / autocomplete / embed / rerank / edit / apply / summarize) can be set,
plus `capabilities` (`tool_use` is required for Agent mode; `image_input` also exists).

Contrast with `./cursor.md`: Cursor can only use models in its catalog; Continue can point at any provider.

**Tool-calling quality after switching across providers:
the official pages give no comparison.**
axes.runtime:
**An IDE-extension form, not a standalone editor.**

The officially listed forms are the VS Code extension and the JetBrains plugin,
plus a **CLI (`cn`)**.

**Official docs first sentence**: "Open source AI code assistant for VS Code and JetBrains"

**Official README recommendation**: "We recommend using the Continue CLI instead of the JetBrains plugin"

The three forms share the same agent core. **Official CLI page wording**: "the same agent that powers the Continue IDE extensions". The CLI needs Node.js 20+ or a bundled runtime.

**This entry covers only the extension form**; the terminal form's capabilities are in tools and background.
axes.local_files:
**Reads and writes inside the IDE workspace; changes are presented as diffs.**

**Context comes from explicit references, not implicit full indexing.**
The official Chat context page lists context providers such as `@Files`, `@Terminal`, `@Git Diff`,
plus highlighted code (VS Code `cmd/ctrl+L`, JetBrains `cmd/ctrl+J`) and the current active file.

Two config directories: MCP at `.continue/mcpServers/`, rules at `.continue/rules`.

**How the codebase semantic index is implemented is not stated by the official side**
(checked the docs.continue.dev homepage and the Chat context-selection pages).
axes.background:
**The extension form has no "keeps running after shutdown" capability.**

It is an editor / IDE plugin, alive with the IDE process; close the IDE and it ends.

The official docs also describe no cloud execution surface (**verified**: checked the docs.continue.dev homepage,
Agent quick-start and CLI quickstart pages)

**The only async form is the CLI's headless mode.**
`cn -p "..."` runs once and outputs to stdout.

**Official wording**: "Use this in scripts, CI/CD, and git hooks"
axes.tools:
**The tool surface is "three mode tiers + MCP".**

The official Agent page shows three options under mode switching:

- Chat (no tools)
- Plan (read-only tools)
- Agent (all tools)

`Cmd/Ctrl + .` cycles through them.

**MCP is officially supported** (official MCP deep-dive page): configured under `mcpServers` in config,
can live in the `.continue/mcpServers/` directory; three transports supported:

- `stdio`
- `sse`
- `streamable-http`

**JSON MCP configs from Claude / Cursor / Cline can be reused directly.**

**The official stresses**: "MCP can only be used in the **agent** mode"

The CLI side additionally has `--mcp <slug>`, `--agent <slug>`, `--rule`.
Extension mechanisms also include context providers, rules and custom prompts.
axes.context:
**Context is explicitly selected, not auto-indexed** (see local_files).

At the session level: the CLI supports `--resume` replay;
the official CLI headless page says `cn -p --resume`

**official wording**: "replays the previous session's history"

**Cross-session long-term memory** is carried by rules, context providers and assistant configuration;
`config.yaml` has a `data` field.

**Context-window size follows the chosen model**; the official gives no unified number on the pages checked
(checked the Agent quick-start and config.yaml reference pages).
axes.permissions:
**Asks per tool by default; policies can loosen it.**

On the IDE side, **official Agent quick-start wording**: "By default, Agent mode will ask permission when it wants to use a tool"

**tool policies** can set specific tools to automatic or excluded.
In the IDE, click `Continue` to allow or `Cancel` to deny.

The CLI side differs. **Official headless page wording**: "tools that would normally prompt for approval (`ask` permission) are automatically excluded";
to write files you must explicitly pass `--allow Write --allow Edit` (or `--allow "*"`),
plus `--readonly` (Plan), `--auto`, `--exclude`.

**telemetry**: the repository README says the final 2.0.0 release came "removing anonymous telemetry".

**Whether data is used for training: not stated on the official pages checked.**
axes.fit:
**Fits three kinds of people:**

- those needing model freedom (multi-provider, including Ollama local models) without single-vendor lock-in.
- those already working in VS Code / JetBrains who want an open-source auditable extension.
- those needing the same agent in the terminal and CI (`cn -p`).

**Not a fit** for scenarios needing continuous maintenance and long-term evolution — the upstream repository is read-only,
the company was acquired by Cursor, and it will only persist as "the code remains freely usable".

Also not a fit for people depending on official support and continuous fixes.

sections.⚠ 当前状态（最重要的前提）:
Keep using it if you like — just stop expecting updates. The official site continue.dev is now an acquisition notice, original wording:

> Continue has been acquired by Cursor... our open-source codebase remains
> freely available as a foundation for others.

Repository README, top-of-file original wording:

> Note: The `continuedev/continue` repository is no longer actively maintained
> and is read-only for all users.

The final released versions are the "final 2.0.0 release" of the VS Code extension, CLI and JetBrains plugin
(`v2.0.0-vscode`, `v2.1.0-vscode` visible in releases).

Per the release notes, the final versions removed the CLI install banner and the "Hub slug",
and added deprecation notices; per the README they also came **"removing anonymous telemetry"**.

| Question | Conclusion |
|---|---|
| Can it still be used? | Yes — the Apache-2.0 code remains public (repository read-only; the official gives no archival date) |
| Will there be updates? | No — the README states "no longer actively maintained" |
| Is the commercial line still around? | The old Hub pricing page is 404; under the continue.dev domain it is now Continuous AI |

| Form | Key capabilities |

sections.模型自配（官方列 30+ provider）:
Providers covered on the official model providers page:

- Anthropic
- Azure AI Foundry
- Amazon Bedrock
- DeepSeek
- Gemini
- Mistral
- **Ollama (local models)**
- OpenAI
- Vertex AI
- xAI

That page also points to "More (30 items)".

Configuration is the `models` block in `config.yaml`; each entry writes `provider` + `model` (+ optional `apiBase`),
with `roles` and `capabilities` specifiable (`tool_use` is a prerequisite for Agent mode).

**This is the most fundamental difference from `./cursor.md`**: Cursor uses models from its catalog,
while Continue can point at any provider, including fully local runs.
sections.MCP 与权限:
MCP officially supports three transports: `stdio`, `sse`, `streamable-http`;
configuration lives in `.continue/mcpServers/`, and **JSON MCP configs from Claude / Cursor / Cline
can be copied in directly**. One hard official limit to note:
"MCP can only be used in the **agent** mode".

Permission stance splits by side:

- **IDE**: official wording "By default, Agent mode will ask permission when it wants
  to use a tool"; tool policies can set tools to automatic or excluded;

- **CLI headless**: official wording "tools that would normally prompt for approval
  (`ask` permission) are automatically excluded"; to write files you must explicitly pass
  `--allow Write` (or `--allow "*"`).
sections.商业线：Continuous AI（与开源扩展分开读）:
hub.continue.dev (fetched 2026-10-08) is now the commercial line **Continuous AI**, three tiers:

| Tier | Highlights |
|---|---|
| Starter | pay-as-you-go: create and run agents, hook up Slack / Sentry / Snyk |
| Team | per-seat subscription (credits per seat): share private agents across the team, Gmail/GitHub SSO |
| Company | custom: SAML/OIDC, BYOK, committed usage / invoicing / SLA |

Price numbers are not stored per D9 policy; see hub.continue.dev/pricing.

**Note this is not a subscription for the IDE extension** — the extension itself is free and open source.

This commercial line has pivoted to Continuous AI centered on PR checks,
no longer "Continue Hub".
sections.核验说明:
This entry is marked `confidence: partial` for three reasons:

- **Official body text obtained**: forms, self-configured models, MCP, permissions, license and the commercial-line structure.
- **Maintenance has stopped**: upstream repository read-only, official site replaced by the acquisition notice; no future updates.
- **No longer verifiable from official pages**: old Hub pricing, the fate of accounts/subscriptions and other historical capabilities.

Official pages verified this round: repository README and Releases, official site continue.dev (incl. the www variant),
docs-site homepage, MCP deep-dive, Model providers, Agent quick-start,
CLI quickstart and CLI headless, commercial-line pricing page hub.continue.dev/pricing.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md).

**Suggested measurement**: focus on two things.

- **Behavioral consistency of the same `config.yaml` across the IDE extension and the CLI (`cn`) forms**
- **The boundary of headless mode auto-excluding `ask`-permission tools** —
  the official is explicit that "with nobody to approve, they are auto-excluded"; this is the easiest tripwire for scripted users.
